summary: King County, WA cupola lookout built 1923 on Pyramid Peak; L-4 cab followed, gone by 1965; 2023 photos show anchors and possible outhouse or cellar.

facts.design: Cupola cabin (1923), later a gable L-4 cab per the register and firelookout.com
facts.status_note: Register says the lookout was gone by 1965; the guide and a 2026 blog say the buildings burned. Anchors and possible outhouse or cellar remain per 2023 photo captions.

access.note: A hiking guide and a blog describe hikes to the summit on gravel roads and a trail; neither mentions a closure. No Forest Service statement was read.

visit.trail_note: Guide: 1 mile hike, gravel road access. Blog: steep 0.7-mile hike up Pyramid Peak Trail #1160. Check current conditions with the Forest Service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say an L-4 cab replaced the cupola in 1948 and the lookout was gone by 1965, with no cause given. The hiking guide says the USFS burned the cupola in 1948 and that an L-4 it may have put up burned in the 1950s or early 1960s. The blog says the L-4 burned in the early 1960s and that the site was no longer in use by 1968. The records do not settle the order of events, so the story gives the accounts side by side.
The register and firelookout.com give 5,715 ft; the hiking guide gives 5,718 ft for the lookout elevation. The story uses 5,715 ft.
The guide gives a 1-mile hike on gravel roads; the blog gives a steep 0.7-mile hike up Pyramid Peak Trail #1160. Neither figure was measured against a map.

sources.title: Pyramid Peak - Tales From the Plateau

notes_for_editor: Brief access was 'unknown'; set to public from the hiking guide and blog, which describe summit hikes and mention no closure. No Forest Service statement was read. Sources disagree on the 1948 to 1965 sequence. The blog is a personal site and is used only for the burn date and the 2011-era outhouse detail. Photo credits were not recorded (no license information was found); the 1937 USFS photo and 1928 photos are not listed as new finds.
